subject: Ad disapproved: Policy violation in "Fall Sale — Search & Shopping"
snippet: Hi Jordan, One or more ads in your account "Habitat Goods — Search & Shopping" (412-908-6631) were disapproved for violating our Misleading Representation policy. This affects the
body_text:
Hi Jordan,

One or more ads in your account "Habitat Goods — Search & Shopping" (412-908-6631) were disapproved for violating our Misleading Representation policy. This affects the "Fall Sale — Up to 50% Off" search campaign, which has been paused for the affected ad group.

WHAT WAS FLAGGED
Ad group: Fall Sale - Broad Match
Headline flagged: "Everything 50% Off — Today Only"
Reason: Our systems found this claim to be misleading because the sitewide discount referenced does not apply to your full catalog, and "today only" language was used across a promotion that has run for 11 consecutive days. This falls under our policy on exaggerated claims and false urgency, which prohibits advertising that creates a false sense of scarcity or time pressure that doesn't reflect the actual offer.

WHAT THIS MEANS
- The disapproved ads will not serve until the issue is resolved.
- Other ads in the same campaign are unaffected and continue to serve normally.
- Repeated policy violations across your account can lead to ad group, campaign, or account-level suspension.

HOW TO FIX IT
1. Edit the disapproved headline to accurately reflect the offer (e.g. reference the actual discount range, such as "Up to 50% Off Select Styles," and remove "today only" if the promotion is ongoing).
2. Resubmit the ad for review. Most reviews complete within 1 business day, though some can take longer.
3. If you believe this was flagged in error, you can request a manual review from the Policy Manager section of your account.

We also flagged two additional headlines in the same ad group as borderline and recommend reviewing your full Fall Sale headline set before resubmitting, to avoid a second review cycle. The borderline headlines were "Last Chance — Ends Tonight" and "Prices This Low Won't Last," both of which use similar urgency framing and are likely to draw the same scrutiny once a human reviewer looks at the ad group following the first disapproval.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Your account currently has a "Good" policy standing, but two disapprovals within a 90-day window can trigger a policy standing downgrade, which can slow down approval times for future campaigns, including your planned Q4 holiday launch. A downgraded account also loses access to some beta features and can see slower turnaround on manual review requests, which matters if you're planning to launch time-sensitive holiday creative in November.

WHAT WE RECOMMEND BEFORE YOU RESUBMIT
- Replace absolute claims ("Everything," "Today Only") with qualified language that matches the actual promotion mechanics in your checkout.
- Make sure any percentage-off claim matches the actual discount code logic — our reviewers now spot-check landing pages against ad copy.
- If the promotion is meant to run for multiple days, avoid "today only," "ends tonight," or countdown-style language unless there's a real countdown timer tied to an actual end date.
- Consider a policy pre-check pass on all Q4 holiday ad copy before launch, given the volume you're planning to run in November and December.

If you have questions, you can reach our policy support team through the Help Center or by replying to this notification with your account ID. Most manual review requests are resolved within 2 business days, but during Q4 ramp-up volume can push that closer to 4-5 business days, so we'd recommend getting ahead of any holiday creative review well before your planned launch dates.

Google Ads Policy Team
This is an automated notification from Google Ads.

The disapproved ads will not serve until resolved. Edit the headline to reflect the actual offer and resubmit for review.

subject: Weekly Anomaly Digest — 3 metrics flagged
snippet: Hi Jordan, Here's your Weekly Anomaly Digest for Habitat Goods (Aug 3 - Aug 9). Three metrics were flagged by our detection models this week. 1. EMAIL-ATTRIBUTED REVENUE — UP 34% E
body_text:
Hi Jordan,

Here's your Weekly Anomaly Digest for Habitat Goods (Aug 3 - Aug 9). Three metrics were flagged by our detection models this week.

1. EMAIL-ATTRIBUTED REVENUE — UP 34%
Email-attributed revenue rose from a weekly average of $61,200 to $82,100, a 34% increase. This tracks with the "Back to School Flash Sale" campaign that went out 7/18 and the follow-up cart abandonment flow Ben set up in June — attribution modeling shows roughly 60% of the lift coming from returning customers who opened but didn't click on the first send, then converted off the second-touch reminder. No action needed here, flagging as a positive anomaly worth noting for the Q4 planning offsite deck.

2. NEW USER SIGNUP RATE — DOWN 12%
New account creation on the site is down 12% week over week, concentrated in organic search traffic (-19%) rather than paid (-3%) or direct (-1%). This lines up with a broader dip in organic sessions that started the week of 7/27, which may be related to a Google core update — worth checking Search Console for ranking movement on your top 20 landing pages. Paid and lifecycle channels are compensating for most of the volume, so total revenue is not currently at risk, but the trend is worth watching for another week before treating it as noise.

3. SESSION DURATION ON PDP (PRODUCT DETAIL PAGE) — DOWN 9%
Average session duration on product detail pages dropped 9%, most visible on the new "Linen Collection" pages that launched 8/1. This could indicate the new page layout is either working very well (fast add-to-cart, less browsing needed) or underperforming (users bouncing quickly). Add-to-cart rate on these pages is flat, and bounce rate is up 4 points, which leans toward the latter explanation. Recommend a quick session-replay review before drawing conclusions.

WHAT WE'D FLAG FOR THE OFFSITE DECK
The email revenue lift (#1) is a good data point for the lifecycle section of the Q4 plan. The organic dip (#2) is worth a line in the risks section even if it resolves on its own — better to have flagged it than not. The PDP session duration change (#3) probably doesn't need its own slide, but worth a footnote if anyone asks why bounce rate ticked up on the new template.

A NOTE ON METHODOLOGY
These anomalies are flagged relative to a rolling 8-week baseline that automatically excludes known promotional spikes (like the Back to School Flash Sale) so seasonal noise doesn't drown out real signal. If a metric you'd expect to see here — like paid social CAC or the lifecycle flow performance Ben has been tuning — isn't included, it's most likely because it's still within one standard deviation of its baseline and didn't clear our flagging threshold this week. You can adjust sensitivity per-metric from the Anomaly Detection settings panel if you'd like tighter or looser thresholds heading into the higher-volume Q4 stretch.

As always, you can dig into any of these in the live dashboard, and this digest will auto-adjust its baselines as more data comes in. If the organic dip hasn't resolved by next week's digest, we'll escalate it from a soft flag to a tracked anomaly with its own trend line.

— The Amplitude Team
This is an automated weekly digest based on your saved dashboards.

subject: Your Weekly Deliverability & Campaign Performance Report
snippet: Hi Jordan, Here's your Weekly Deliverability & Campaign Performance Report for Habitat Goods, covering July 27 - August 2. CAMPAIGNS SENT THIS WEEK: 4 - "Weekend Linen Sale" (8/1)
body_text:
Hi Jordan,

Here's your Weekly Deliverability & Campaign Performance Report for Habitat Goods, covering July 27 - August 2.

CAMPAIGNS SENT THIS WEEK: 4
- "Weekend Linen Sale" (8/1) — 88,204 sent, 24.1% open, 3.8% click
- "New Arrivals: Fall Textiles" (7/30) — 84,910 sent, 21.7% open, 3.1% click
- "Cart Reminder Flow" (ongoing) — 12,340 sent, 38.2% open, 9.4% click
- "Restock Alert: Harlow Sofa" (7/28) — 6,102 sent, 41.0% open, 12.7% click

DELIVERABILITY HEALTH: GOOD
Your sender score is currently 94/100, up from 91 last week. Inbox placement across major providers:
- Gmail: 97.2%
- Yahoo/AOL: 88.4% (recovering — was 81.1% two weeks ago after the spam complaint spike)
- Outlook/Hotmail: 95.8%
- iCloud: 96.1%

LIST HEALTH
Active profiles: 412,880 (+2,140 net this week)
Unsubscribes: 890 (0.21% of sends — within normal range)
Spam complaints: 118 (0.028% of sends — back under the 0.1% threshold after last week's alert)
Suppressed (bounced/complained): 1,204

SEGMENT PERFORMANCE
Your "VIP — Repeat Purchasers" segment continues to outperform, at 41% open / 11% click across all sends this week, roughly 2x the account average. The "Win-back — 90 Day Lapsed" flow saw a modest lift after the subject line change Ben tested last week (from "We miss you" to "Your cart's still here + 15% off") — open rate up from 14% to 19%. The "Restock Alert" flow remains your highest-converting automation by a wide margin, and given the Harlow Sofa's performance this week, it might be worth expanding the trigger list to a few more high-demand SKUs ahead of the holiday season.

FLOW-LEVEL NOTES
- Welcome Series (5 emails): 52% average open, steady week over week, no changes recommended.
- Cart Abandonment (3 emails): 38% open on message 1, dropping to 22% by message 3 — consider testing a stronger incentive on the final touch.
- Post-Purchase (2 emails): open rates healthy, but click-to-review-request is only 4%, worth a design refresh if review volume is a Q4 priority.

WHAT WE'D FLAG
Your Yahoo/AOL placement is recovering well after last week's deliverability alert, but we'd recommend holding off on any high-frequency sends to that segment specifically for another 1-2 weeks until placement is fully back above 90%. In the meantime, it's worth trimming your least-engaged Yahoo/AOL profiles (no opens in 180 days) out of general campaign sends and routing them to a lighter-touch win-back track instead — that alone should help placement recover faster than time alone would. Everything else is healthy and trending in the right direction heading into Q4 planning, and your account-wide sender score of 94 puts you comfortably in our top tier of senders by volume.

Full report and segment-level detail available in your Klaviyo dashboard.

— The Klaviyo Team
